Instead, Mydei simply returns the basket when she offers it to him. “Thank you for your generosity. But I cannot answer any prayers myself—I can only tell you where I might…recommend paying a visit.”

After he sees a more-confident Metea on her way (she wouldn’t take back the honeycakes, so he now has a snack as well), he walks back into the foyer only to see a smiling Phainon leaning against one of the pillars there, arms folded over his chest. “Well…she seemed in better sprits when she left. Did you tell her about a certain tree?”

“I may have suggested praying there,” Mydei replies, deliberately keeping his wording vague to match Phainon’s. “But I didn’t say what happened exactly. I think she’ll have to figure the rest out on her own.”

“And I hope that she does, so she can experience what she wants too,” Phainon murmurs, as he loops his arms around him and pulls him in for an embrace. “But my, I wonder if she’ll be the only one…do you think we’re going to have to pray to you as the new Titan of Fertility?”

He receives a swift blow to the gut for that.
